doc.title: laying_grass — Noa Tournoy
doc.desc: laying_grass: a tile-laying game in pure C++17 with zero dependencies — standard library only, right down to the hand-written JSON parser. 96 tile shapes, 2 to 9 players.
lede: A tile-laying game inspired by "The Devil's Plan", written in pure C++17: standard library only, right down to the JSON parser.
sujet.1: The game reads its 96 tile shapes from a JSON file. Pulling in a library to read one file would have been quicker to write; the parser is hand-written instead. That is the decision that sums up the project, and the one that teaches the most.
sujet.2: Two to nine players, on a 20 × 20 or 30 × 30 grid depending on the count, nine rounds each. Tiles rotate and flip. The winner is whoever holds the largest filled square at the end; ties are broken by total territory.
archi.p: A clean separation between rules, placement validation, algorithms and display. Game holds the logic, Validator decides whether a move is legal, Algorithms carries the largest-square search and the connectivity computation, Board manages the grid and territories. RAII, enum class, constexpr, STL: the language's own tools rather than patches.
archi.p2: Three bonus mechanics sit on top of placement: exchange coupons, which let you pick from the next five tiles; stones, which block an opponent; and annexation, which takes a cell from the territory across the board.
archi.p3: The repository is documented separately: getting started, architecture and implementation decisions, detailed rules, file tree and inter-module dependencies.
colo.face: Set in Roboto Flex, opsz, wght, wdth and GRAD axes, subset to Latin, 235 KB. Scrolling holds the slider.
colo.hand: Written by hand. One library, GSAP, served from this domain. No third-party requests, no tracker. The text reads without JavaScript.
